description.narrative:
The most important project level outcomes are: (i) Economy wide effects: The Project which will support the expansion and modernization of the hotel is expected to have various positive economy-wide effects including: (a) direct job creation/preservation and contribution to GDP during the construction and operation phase of the hotel as well as indirect effects across the supply chains; (b) higher tax revenues for local government; (c) provision of infrastructure supporting the development of the tourism sector; and (d) increase in economic activities through increased international arrivals. These benefits will be important in South Sudan, where unemployment rates, exports are heavily dominated by oil and tourism & travel represent a small share of the GDP; and (ii) Stakeholder impacts: (a) Employees: The Project will also contribute to local skill development. Dembesh Hotel will provide training to all its employees, addressing the skills gap and (b) benefit local suppliers through increased linkages.
Beyond the Project, IFC anticipates that the investment will facilitate market creation in terms of: (i) Competitiveness: The Project is anticipated to be the second internationally branded hotel to enter the market, contributing to the development of the countrys business infrastructure; and (ii) Integration: The Project has the potential to promote integration of local suppliers within domestic supply chains. As suppliers receive training and contingent to level of training they receive, they can expand their reach beyond the hotel and start working with other local players.

The proposed investment is an up to US$3.75 million IFC A loan (IFC Loan) and an up to US$3.75 million IDA PSW Subordinated Loan (PSW Loan) (jointly the Loans) to Dembesh Hotel South Sudan Ltd (Dembesh Hotel or the Hotel). Dembesh Hotel is an independent owner operating a 50-key business hotel in Juba, the capital city of South Sudan. The Loans will be used to finance part of the Hotels US$20.05 million project involving a 30-room extension and refurbishment of the existing rooms (the Project). The balance of the funding will be provided by the majority shareholder Mr. Ayesheshim Teka Zeleke (the Sponsor).
